stories.body: Yemen's Houthi movement said it launched dozens of drones and ballistic missiles at military facilities and infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including bases, radar sites, runways and ammunition depots. The claims came as government forces reported advances in western Taiz after repelling a Houthi offensive, backed by Saudi-led air strikes. Renewed fighting has displaced nearly 86,000 people in recent weeks, while Houthi gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast and on strategic islands have strengthened their position near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a waterway crucial to global trade and an increasingly important route for Saudi oil exports.
stories.headline: Houthi escalation in Yemen threatens Red Sea shipping and Saudi infrastructure

stories.body: Brent crude rose above $108 a barrel after drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to close its East-West crude pipeline, with traders warning the kingdom's export stocks could be depleted within days unless the line reopens. The disruption follows Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and their capture of Perim Island near the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Markets were also unsettled by the postponement of Gulf talks with Tehran on a temporary shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, while higher oil and gas prices add to inflation pressure ahead of central-bank decisions in several major economies.
stories.headline: Oil prices rise after drone attacks shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline

stories.body: An Iranian cargo vessel was struck near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one person and injuring four, according to Iranian state media. Tehran blamed what it described as a terrorist enemy. The incident comes amid mounting threats to shipping around both Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, while Oman has delayed talks between Iran and Gulf states that had been intended to address the regional maritime crisis.
stories.headline: Iranian cargo ship struck near the Strait of Hormuz as regional talks are delayed

stories.body: Sweden's centre-left opposition held a narrow lead over the governing right-wing bloc as counting continued after the general election. With most votes counted, the opposition was projected to win 176 seats in the 349-seat parliament, against 173 for the right, though late postal and overseas ballots mean the final result may not be known until later in the week. Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson said her bloc was leading but urged patience, while Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said the question of who will govern remained open.
stories.headline: Sweden's centre-left bloc holds a razor-thin lead after the general election

stories.body: A Russian drone hit the engine of a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, around two kilometres from Ukraine's border with Poland, after passengers had been evacuated and with no casualties reported. Former British prime minister Boris Johnson and several European security figures had travelled along the same rail line after a conference in Kyiv, while former CIA director David Petraeus was at the station around the time of the strike. Ukraine's rail operator said the diplomatic train may have been the intended target, and officials in Kyiv and Warsaw condemned the attack as an escalation close to NATO territory.
stories.headline: Russia strikes a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine's border with Poland

stories.body: Indonesian rescue teams have deployed specialist underwater personnel and navy-operated underwater drones as they search for more than 120 people missing after the Virgo Transport 8 ferry capsized in the Java Sea. The operation is intensifying as authorities seek to locate survivors and investigate the circumstances of the disaster.
stories.headline: Search expands for more than 120 people missing after a ferry capsizes in Indonesia's Java Sea

stories.body: AI-related shares fell across Asia and Europe after Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei called rapid development reckless and warned that advanced AI agents could eventually cause vast damage. SoftBank shares fell 13%, South Korea's Kospi dropped 3%, and semiconductor-linked companies including ASML and Taiwan Semiconductor also declined. OpenAI's Sam Altman, Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis and SpaceX's Elon Musk expressed support for slowing development, but critics said the proposal lacks a clear definition or enforceable international mechanism, particularly amid competition with China.
stories.headline: AI-linked stocks fall as industry leaders call for a slowdown in development

stories.body: Former President Barack Obama has urged Democrats to develop a comprehensive AI agenda, warning that the technology is advancing rapidly in private hands and could be dangerous without effective oversight. At a private fundraiser, Obama said a presidential AI plan should address safety, risks to children, job displacement and the social safety net, while encouraging Congress to frame a public debate on regulation. His comments add to pressure on Democrats and lawmakers more broadly as AI industry leaders call for stronger safeguards and the Trump administration emphasizes US competition with China.
stories.headline: Obama urges Democrats to make AI safety, jobs and regulation a central policy agenda

stories.body: A growing number of election-related lawsuits is creating uncertainty only weeks before the US midterm elections, with courts still resolving disputes that could affect how voting is conducted. The late-stage legal activity is contributing to confusion for election officials and voters as key rules remain contested.
stories.headline: Election lawsuits create uncertainty weeks before the US midterm elections

stories.body: A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's plan to cut the Federal Emergency Management Agency by 50% was unlawful, saying the Department of Homeland Security proposal appeared to have been pulled from thin air. The judge found that the reduction would impair FEMA's ability to carry out its legally required mission to respond to disasters.
stories.headline: Federal judge rules Trump administration plan to cut FEMA by half unlawful

stories.body: The judicial fallout from the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta is deepening as the National Court investigates events surrounding the crisis and considers allegations over whether authorities acted on warnings. A judge has asked to take over a related local inquiry involving the government's delegate in Ceuta, while political opponents are seeking to extend scrutiny to the national government. The crisis, in which more than 70,000 people crossed from Morocco over two days and at least 141 people died, continues to shape Spanish politics and debate over Morocco's role.
stories.headline: Spain's Ceuta migration crisis moves deeper into the courts

stories.body: Spain's Central Electoral Board is meeting to determine how to apply a Supreme Court order that provisionally suspended voting rights for people naturalized under the Democratic Memory Law, often known as the grandchildren law. The measure concerns descendants of Spaniards exiled during the Civil War and has prompted a dispute over whether the board may address the underlying legal issue or must only decide where and how affected voters would cast ballots. Digital Transformation Minister Óscar López called the suspension a democratic outrage and accused sectors of the judiciary of seeking to undermine the government.
stories.headline: Spain's electoral board considers how to implement the Supreme Court order on the Democratic Memory 'grandchildren law'

stories.body: Justice Minister Félix Bolaños has appealed the General Council of the Judiciary's decision to dismiss his complaints about Judge Juan Carlos Peinado, accusing the judicial governing body of corporatism and conservatism. Bolaños cited issues including Peinado's questioning of him as a witness, an unsuccessful request to investigate him, and alleged leaks to the press. The council concluded in August that disciplinary action was not appropriate because the matters fell within judicial activity, but Bolaños says he will take the case to the Supreme Court.
stories.headline: Justice Minister Félix Bolaños challenges the judiciary over its dismissal of his complaint against Judge Peinado

stories.body: French President Emmanuel Macron will make a state visit to Spain on September 29 and 30, with a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez scheduled at the Moncloa Palace. Macron and his wife, Brigitte Macron, will also be received by Spain's king and queen for a state dinner. The visit comes amid the Ceuta migration crisis and while a bilateral friendship and cooperation treaty signed in 2023 remains unratified because of controversy over provisions for ministers to attend the other country's cabinet meetings.
stories.headline: Macron will make a state visit to Spain on September 29 and 30

stories.body: A three-bedroom Barcelona apartment advertised at about €1,000 a month received roughly 1,800 applications in less than an hour, illustrating the severe mismatch between rental supply and demand. The successful tenants paid €911 in rent plus property-tax and community charges, while reporting that an estate agent charged them €242 for management and utility-transfer services that residential tenants should not have to pay. Property administrators say the volume of applications is increasingly leading agents and landlords to use AI to filter potential tenants, with applicants often required to provide extensive financial and employment records.
stories.headline: Barcelona rental listing draws nearly 2,000 applications in an hour, highlighting the housing crunch

stories.body: Residents and businesses displaced by the L9 sinkhole in Barcelona's Sant Gervasi neighbourhood are preparing a collective lawsuit against the Catalan government, seeking material, economic and moral damages. More than two months after the sinkhole forced around 300 residents and traders to leave, 18 households remain displaced and some businesses may be unable to reopen until January. The Generalitat says it will create a permanent support office for people affected by the works while its investigation continues, acknowledging that public authorities must respond to residents who did not cause the disruption.
stories.headline: Residents displaced by the L9 sinkhole prepare a collective lawsuit as Catalonia plans a permanent support office

stories.body: Rodalies has launched a new mobile app that gives users real-time service information, train location tracking, online ticket purchases and interactive maps. The Renfe-backed platform also includes AI-assisted route searches, personalized content based on travel habits, voice search, saved journeys and accessibility improvements. It replaces the existing Rodalies app, which stops operating on September 15.
stories.headline: Rodalies launches a new app with real-time train tracking and service information
